label: rem:alpha-em-categorical-trace-ratio-interpretation
title: Interpretation: $\alpha_{EM}$ as $h^2$ over force-carrier categorical traces, and its role in the Hartree-energy conjecture
html:
Interpretation. The trace-ratio identity (\alpha_{EM} categorical trace-ratio) refactors \alpha_{EM} from the inverse Bring complex complexity into the ratio of h^{2} over the product of force-carrier categorical traces. This shifts the \alpha_{EM} formula from an operator-selection-LP-cost interpretation to the q-dimension layer.

The structural picture requires two components:

  • For each force carrier, the \delta_q-decoration evaluates to a pure categorical trace \delta_q(T_{p,q}) = q^{q} - q^{-q} in the appropriate p-strand realisation.
  • The inverse product of these two traces, rescaled by h^{2}/q, yields \alpha_{EM}.

The h^{2} numerator originates from the two (q - q^{-1}) factors in the denominators of [9]_q and [10]_q.

Significance for the Hartree-energy conjecture. This identity supplies the algebraic mechanism introducing \alpha_{EM}^{2} into the binding energy. The molecular bound state projects onto the Wedderburn channels (3, 1) and (2, 1, 1) with non-trivial \delta_q weight (prop:force-carrier-intertwining-correspondence).

Squaring the trace-ratio identity yields:

  \alpha_{EM}^{2}
  \;=\;
  \frac{h^{4}}{q^{2} \cdot \delta_q(T_{2,9})^{2} \cdot \delta_q(T_{3,5})^{2}}.

The bound-state Markov trace contribution is bilinear in the characters \chi_{(3,1)} and \chi_{(2,1,1)}. Conjecturally, these characters are proportional to \delta_q(T_{3,5})^{-1} and \delta_q(T_{2,9})^{-1}. This bilinearity provides the categorical analogue of the Coulomb potential. Their product supplies the \alpha_{EM}^{2} factor.

Closing this algebraic identity constitutes the next step for conj:e-hartree-categorical-derivation.
